## Historical audit: S0085

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; observations were not split across chunks.

| Aspect | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct a photographed indoor scene with separate editable meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, geometry and materials. The student’s kitchen interpretation is an inference from its program, not independent inspection of the reference (line 1, student `model_request`; line 3, student `model_response`). |
| First build | The executed program constructs multiple assets: room, beams, posts, cabinets, island, sink and tap, cooktop, extractor and kettle. It groups constituent meshes, uses procedural wood and extractor bump materials, and sets camera and lights. Grouping is evidence of intended part association, not verified physical contact or connection; object pose and placement are coded estimates (lines 3–4). |
| Review and revision | After receiving step 1’s render and a general comparison prompt, the student diagnosed a distant, frontal view, narrow island end, central post and washed-out dark regions. Step 2 changed camera position and height, island dimensions and post placement, extended cabinetry, and reduced lighting while retaining the lens (lines 7, 9–10). These diagnoses are student claims, not independent visual verification. |
| Camera obstruction | The student subsequently reported that step 2 showed only a wall and attributed this to the camera being outside the left wall. Step 3 moved the camera inside, omitted that wall, restored island width and repositioned objects; this proposed repair was actually executed (lines 15–16). The wall-only result and its diagnosis cannot be independently checked from the supplied text. |
| Validation and selection | All three executions report `ok: true`, saved renders and blend files; render logs show 16 samples despite larger values in the programs. Step 3 was selected automatically and then explicitly by the student after the render budget was exhausted (lines 5–6, 11–12, 17–18, 19, 21–22). Execution success is not proof of visual or geometric correctness. |
| Teacher and autonomy | No teacher-specific detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible. The user/runner supplied generic review instructions and render results, which the student received; the subsequent diagnoses and revisions are the student’s own. Sessions report no tool calls, although the external runner executed the three builds (lines 7–8, 13–14, 19–20). |

**Outcome:** Successful execution and final selection of step 3; overall reconstruction correctness remains **unknown**, not a demonstrated formal visual success. There was no empty patch or visible technical interruption. Step 2’s claimed occlusion is an apparent scene/camera failure despite successful rendering.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable lesson is to distinguish a successful render operation from a usable view and to check camera obstruction during iteration. The kitchen inventory, post crop and lighting adjustments are task-specific. Without the actual images or independent geometric checks, whether step 3 corrected the obstruction, matched perspective and materials, connected parts convincingly, or improved on step 1 remains unresolved.
